function.name: patch
function.description:
Targeted find-and-replace edits in files. Use this instead of sed/awk in terminal. Uses fuzzy matching (9 strategies) so minor whitespace/indentation differences won't break it. Returns a unified diff. Auto-runs syntax checks after editing.

Replace mode (default): find a unique string and replace it.
Patch mode: apply V4A multi-file patches for bulk changes.

mode.description: Edit mode: 'replace' for targeted find-and-replace, 'patch' for V4A multi-file patches

path.description: File path to edit (required for 'replace' mode)

old_string.description: Text to find in the file (required for 'replace' mode). Must be unique in the file unless replace_all=true. Include enough surrounding context to ensure uniqueness.

new_string.description: Replacement text (required for 'replace' mode). Can be empty string to delete the matched text.

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences instead of requiring a unique match (default: false)

patch.description:
V4A format patch content (required for 'patch' mode). Format:
*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: path/to/file
@@ context hint @@
 context line
-removed line
+added line
*** End Patch

function.name: process
function.description: Manage background processes started with terminal(background=true). Actions: 'list' (show all), 'poll' (check status + new output), 'log' (full output with pagination), 'wait' (block until done or timeout), 'kill' (terminate), 'write' (send raw stdin data without newline), 'submit' (send data + Enter, for answering prompts).

action.description: Action to perform on background processes

session_id.description: Process session ID (from terminal background output). Required for all actions except 'list'.

data.description: Text to send to process stdin (for 'write' and 'submit' actions)

timeout.description: Max seconds to block for 'wait' action. Returns partial output on timeout.

offset.description: Line offset for 'log' action (default: last 200 lines)

limit.description: Max lines to return for 'log' action

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with line numbers and pagination. Use this instead of cat/head/tail in terminal. Output format: 'LINE_NUM|CONTENT'. Suggests similar filenames if not found. Use offset and limit for large files. Reads exceeding ~100K characters are rejected; use offset and limit to read specific sections of large files. NOTE: Cannot read images or binary files — use vision_analyze for images.

path.description: Path to the file to read (absolute, relative, or ~/path)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed, default: 1)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read (default: 500, max: 2000)

function.name: search_files
function.description:
Search file contents or find files by name. Use this instead of grep/rg/find/ls in terminal. Ripgrep-backed, faster than shell equivalents.

Content search (target='content'): Regex search inside files. Output modes: full matches with line numbers, file paths only, or match counts.

File search (target='files'): Find files by glob pattern (e.g., '*.py', '*config*'). Also use this instead of ls — results sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: Regex pattern for content search, or glob pattern (e.g., '*.py') for file search

target.description: 'content' searches inside file contents, 'files' searches for files by name

path.description: Directory or file to search in (default: current working directory)

file_glob.description: Filter files by pattern in grep mode (e.g., '*.py' to only search Python files)

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 50)

offset.description: Skip first N results for pagination (default: 0)

output_mode.description: Output format for grep mode: 'content' shows matching lines with line numbers, 'files_only' lists file paths, 'count' shows match counts per file

context.description: Number of context lines before and after each match (grep mode only)

function.name: terminal
function.description:
Execute shell commands on a Linux environment. Filesystem usually persists between calls.

Do NOT use cat/head/tail to read files — use read_file instead.
Do NOT use grep/rg/find to search — use search_files instead.
Do NOT use ls to list directories — use search_files(target='files') instead.
Do NOT use sed/awk to edit files — use patch instead.
Do NOT use echo/cat heredoc to create files — use write_file instead.
Reserve terminal for: builds, installs, git, processes, scripts, network, package managers, and anything that needs a shell.

Foreground (default): Commands return INSTANTLY when done, even if the timeout is high. Set timeout=300 for long builds/scripts — you'll still get the result in seconds if it's fast. Prefer foreground for everything that finishes.
Background: ONLY for long-running servers, watchers, or processes that never exit. Set background=true to get a session_id, then use process(action="wait") to block until done — it returns instantly on completion, same as foreground. Use process(action="poll") only when you need a progress check without blocking.
Do NOT use background for scripts, builds, or installs — foreground with a generous timeout is always better (fewer tool calls, instant results).
Working directory: Use 'workdir' for per-command cwd.
PTY mode: Set pty=true for interactive CLI tools (Codex, Claude Code, Python REPL).

Do NOT use vim/nano/interactive tools without pty=true — they hang without a pseudo-terminal. Pipe git output to cat if it might page.
Important: cloud sandboxes may be cleaned up, idled out, or recreated between turns. Persistent filesystem means files can resume later; it does NOT guarantee a continuously running machine or surviving background processes. Use terminal sandboxes for task work, not durable hosting.

command.description: The command to execute on the VM

background.description: ONLY for servers/watchers that never exit. For scripts, builds, installs — use foreground with timeout instead (it returns instantly when done).

timeout.description: Max seconds to wait (default: 180). Returns INSTANTLY when command finishes — set high for long tasks, you won't wait unnecessarily.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command (absolute path). Defaults to the session working directory.

check_interval.description: Seconds between automatic status checks for background processes (gateway/messaging only, minimum 30). When set, I'll proactively report progress.

pty.description: Run in pseudo-terminal (PTY) mode for interactive CLI tools like Codex, Claude Code, or Python REPL. Only works with local and SSH backends. Default: false.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Write content to a file, completely replacing existing content. Use this instead of echo/cat heredoc in terminal. Creates parent directories automatically. OVERWRITES the entire file — use 'patch' for targeted edits.

path.description: Path to the file to write (will be created if it doesn't exist, overwritten if it does)

content.description: Complete content to write to the file

### Changes

Add two optional fields to `ToolDefinition`:

- **`shortDescription`** — one-liner for the system prompt tool list (falls back to first line of `description`)
- **`systemGuidelines`** — bullet points appended to the system prompt guidelines section

Custom tools now appear in the system prompt alongside built-ins, with stable ordering: built-ins first (fixed order), then custom tools alphabetically. Guidelines are deduplicated via Set.

**Example:**
```typescript
pi.registerTool({
  name: "my_tool",
  description: "Manage a todo list. Supports listing, adding, and removing items.",
  shortDescription: "Manage a todo list",
  systemGuidelines: ["Confirm with the user before removing todo items"],
  // ...
});
```

Produces:
```
Available tools:
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- my_tool: Manage a todo list

Guidelines:
- Use read to examine files before editing...
- Confirm with the user before removing todo items
```

# Extension Examples

Example extensions for pi-coding-agent.

## Usage

```bash
# Load an extension with --extension flag
pi --extension examples/extensions/permission-gate.ts

# Or copy to extensions directory for auto-discovery
cp permission-gate.ts ~/.pi/agent/extensions/
```

## Examples

### Lifecycle & Safety

| Extension | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `permission-gate.ts` | Prompts for confirmation before dangerous bash commands (rm -rf, sudo, etc.) |
| `protected-paths.ts` | Blocks writes to protected paths (.env, .git/, node_modules/) |
| `confirm-destructive.ts` | Confirms before destructive session actions (clear, switch, fork) |
| `dirty-repo-guard.ts` | Prevents session changes with uncommitted git changes |
| `sandbox/` | OS-level sandboxing using `@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime` with per-project config |

### Custom Tools

| Extension | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `todo.ts` | Todo list tool + `/todos` command with custom rendering and state persistence |
| `hello.ts` | Minimal custom tool example |
| `question.ts` | Demonstrates `ctx.ui.select()` for asking the user questions with custom UI |
| `questionnaire.ts` | Multi-question input with tab bar navigation between questions |
| `tool-override.ts` | Override built-in tools (e.g., add logging/access control to `read`) |
| `built-in-tool-renderer.ts` | Custom compact rendering for built-in tools (read, bash, edit, write) while keeping original behavior |
| `minimal-mode.ts` | Override built-in tool rendering for minimal display (only tool calls, no output in collapsed mode) |
| `truncated-tool.ts` | Wraps ripgrep with proper output truncation (50KB/2000 lines) |
| `antigravity-image-gen.ts` | Generate images via Google Antigravity with optional save-to-disk modes |
| `ssh.ts` | Delegate all tools to a remote machine via SSH using pluggable operations |
| `subagent/` | Delegate tasks to specialized subagents with isolated context windows |

### Commands & UI

| Extension | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `preset.ts` | Named presets for model, thinking level, tools, and instructions via `--preset` flag and `/preset` command |
| `plan-mode/` | Claude Code-style plan mode for read-only exploration with `/plan` command and step tracking |
| `tools.ts` | Interactive `/tools` command to enable/disable tools with session persistence |
| `handoff.ts` | Transfer context to a new focused session via `/handoff <goal>` |
| `qna.ts` | Extracts questions from last response into editor via `ctx.ui.setEditorText()` |
| `status-line.ts` | Shows turn progress in footer via `ctx.ui.setStatus()` with themed colors |
| `widget-placement.ts` | Shows widgets above and below the editor via `ctx.ui.setWidget()` placement |
| `model-status.ts` | Shows model changes in status bar via `model_select` hook |
| `snake.ts` | Snake game with custom UI, keyboard handling, and session persistence |
| `send-user-message.ts` | Demonstrates `pi.sendUserMessage()` for sending user messages from extensions |
| `timed-confirm.ts` | Demonstrates AbortSignal for auto-dismissing `ctx.ui.confirm()` and `ctx.ui.select()` dialogs |
| `rpc-demo.ts` | Exercises all RPC-supported extension UI methods; pair with [`examples/rpc-extension-ui.ts`](../rpc-extension-ui.ts) |
| `modal-editor.ts` | Custom vim-like modal editor via `ctx.ui.setEditorComponent()` |
| `rainbow-editor.ts` | Animated rainbow text effect via custom editor |
| `notify.ts` | Desktop notifications via OSC 777 when agent finishes (Ghostty, iTerm2, WezTerm) |
| `titlebar-spinner.ts` | Braille spinner animation in terminal title while the agent is working |
| `summarize.ts` | Summarize conversation with GPT-5.2 and show in transient UI |
| `custom-footer.ts` | Custom footer with git branch and token stats via `ctx.ui.setFooter()` |
| `custom-header.ts` | Custom header via `ctx.ui.setHeader()` |
| `overlay-test.ts` | Test overlay compositing with inline text inputs and edge cases |
| `overlay-qa-tests.ts` | Comprehensive overlay QA tests: anchors, margins, stacking, overflow, animation |
| `doom-overlay/` | DOOM game running as an overlay at 35 FPS (demonstrates real-time game rendering) |
| `shutdown-command.ts` | Adds `/quit` command demonstrating `ctx.shutdown()` |
| `reload-runtime.ts` | Adds `/reload-runtime` and `reload_runtime` tool showing safe reload flow |
| `interactive-shell.ts` | Run interactive commands (vim, htop) with full terminal via `user_bash` hook |
| `inline-bash.ts` | Expands `!{command}` patterns in prompts via `input` event transformation |

| Extension | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `git-checkpoint.ts` | Creates git stash checkpoints at each turn for code restoration on fork |
| `auto-commit-on-exit.ts` | Auto-commits on exit using last assistant message for commit message |

### System Prompt & Compaction

| Extension | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `pirate.ts` | Demonstrates `systemPromptAppend` to dynamically modify system prompt |
| `claude-rules.ts` | Scans `.claude/rules/` folder and lists rules in system prompt |
| `custom-compaction.ts` | Custom compaction that summarizes entire conversation |
| `trigger-compact.ts` | Triggers compaction when context usage exceeds 100k tokens and adds `/trigger-compact` command |

| Extension | Description |

### Resources

| `custom-provider-gitlab-duo/` | GitLab Duo provider using pi-ai's built-in Anthropic/OpenAI streaming via proxy |

| Extension | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `with-deps/` | Extension with its own package.json and dependencies (demonstrates jiti module resolution) |
| `file-trigger.ts` | Watches a trigger file and injects contents into conversation |

## Writing Extensions

See [docs/extensions.md](../../docs/extensions.md) for full documentation.

```typescript
import type { ExtensionAPI } from "@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent";
import { Type } from "@sinclair/typebox";

export default function (pi: ExtensionAPI) {
  // Subscribe to lifecycle events
  pi.on("tool_call", async (event, ctx) => {
    if (event.toolName === "bash" && event.input.command?.includes("rm -rf")) {
      const ok = await ctx.ui.confirm("Dangerous!", "Allow rm -rf?");
      if (!ok) return { block: true, reason: "Blocked by user" };
    }
  });

  // Register custom tools
  pi.registerTool({
    name: "greet",
    label: "Greeting",
    description: "Generate a greeting",
    parameters: Type.Object({
      name: Type.String({ description: "Name to greet" }),
    }),
    async execute(toolCallId, params, onUpdate, ctx, signal) {
      return {
        content: [{ type: "text", text: `Hello, ${params.name}!` }],
        details: {},
      };
    },
  });

  // Register commands
  pi.registerCommand("hello", {
    description: "Say hello",
    handler: async (args, ctx) => {
      ctx.ui.notify("Hello!", "info");
    },
  });
}
```

## Key Patterns

**Use StringEnum for string parameters** (required for Google API compatibility):
```typescript
import { StringEnum } from "@mariozechner/pi-ai";

// Good
action: StringEnum(["list", "add"] as const)

// Bad - doesn't work with Google
action: Type.Union([Type.Literal("list"), Type.Literal("add")])
```

**State persistence via details:**
```typescript
// Store state in tool result details for proper forking support
return {
  content: [{ type: "text", text: "Done" }],
  details: { todos: [...todos], nextId },  // Persisted in session
};

// Reconstruct on session events
pi.on("session_start", async (_event, ctx) => {
  for (const entry of ctx.sessionManager.getBranch()) {
    if (entry.type === "message" && entry.message.toolName === "my_tool") {
      const details = entry.message.details;
      // Reconstruct state from details
    }
  }
});
```

```typescript
// Bad - doesn't work with Google

```

```typescript

return {
  content: [{ type: "text", text: "Done" }],
  details: { todos: [...todos], nextId },  // Persisted in session
};

  for (const entry of ctx.sessionManager.getBranch()) {
    if (entry.type === "message" && entry.message.toolName === "my_tool") {
      const details = entry.message.details;
      // Reconstruct state from details
    }
  }
});
```

{"content":""""Pydantic models for request/response schemas."""

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, field_validator
from typing import Optional
from datetime import datetime
from enum import Enum


# ── Enums ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

class WeatherCondition(str, Enum):
    CLEAR = "clear"
    CLOUDY = "cloudy"
    RAIN = "rain"
    SNOW = "snow"
    STORM = "storm"
    FOG = "fog"
    WINDY = "windy"


class TemperatureUnit(str, Enum):
    CELSIUS = "celsius"
    FAHRENHEIT = "fahrenheit"


class AggregationType(str, Enum):
    AVERAGE = "average"
    MIN = "min"
    MAX = "max"


# ── Request Models ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

class WeatherRequest(BaseModel):
    """Request model for querying weather data by city."""
    city: str = Field(..., min_length=1, max_length=100, description="City name")
    country_code: Optional[str] = Field(
        None, min_length=2, max_length=2, description="ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code"
    )
    unit: TemperatureUnit = Field(TemperatureUnit.CELSIUS, description="Temperature unit")


class AggregationRequest(BaseModel):
    """Request model for aggregating weather across multiple cities."""
    cities: list[str] = Field(..., min_length=1, max_length=20, description="List of city names")
    aggregation: AggregationType = Field(
        AggregationType.AVERAGE, description="Aggregation method"
    )
    unit: TemperatureUnit = Field(TemperatureUnit.CELSIUS, description="Temperature unit")

    @field_validator("cities")
    @classmethod
    def cities_must_not_be_empty(cls, v: list[str]) -> list[str]:
        stripped = [c.strip() for c in v if c.strip()]
        if not stripped:
            raise ValueError("At least one non-empty city name is required")
        return stripped


# ── Response Models ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

class WeatherData(BaseModel):
    """Core weather data for a single location."""
    city: str
    country: Optional[str] = None
    temperature: float = Field(..., description="Temperature in requested unit")
    feels_like: float = Field(..., description="Feels-like temperature")
    humidity: int = Field(..., ge=0, le=100, description="Humidity percentage")
    pressure: int = Field(..., description="Atmospheric pressure in hPa")
    wind_speed: float = Field(..., ge=0, description="Wind speed in km/h")
    condition: WeatherCondition
    description: str
    visibility: Optional[float] = Field(None, ge=0, description="Visibility in km")
    uv_index: Optional[float] = Field(None, ge=0, description="UV index")
    timestamp: datetime


class WeatherResponse(BaseModel):
    """Single-city weather response."""
    success: bool = True
    data: WeatherData
    unit: TemperatureUnit
    source: str = Field(..., description="Data source identifier")


class AggregationResponse(BaseModel):
    """Multi-city aggregated weather response."""
    success: bool = True
    aggregation: AggregationType
    unit: TemperatureUnit
    aggregated: dict
    city_count: int
    cities: list[str]
    details: list[WeatherData]
    timestamp: datetime


class ForecastDay(BaseModel):
    """Single day forecast."""
    date: str
    temp_high: float
    temp_low: float
    condition: WeatherCondition
    description: str
    precipitation_chance: int = Field(..., ge=0, le=100)


class ForecastResponse(BaseModel):
    """Multi-day forecast response."""
    success: bool = True
    city: str
    unit: TemperatureUnit
    forecast: list[ForecastDay]


class ErrorResponse(BaseModel):
    """Standard error response."""
    success: bool = False
    error: str
    detail: Optional[str] = None
    status_code: int

{"content":""""Weather data service layer — simulated data sources & aggregation logic.

In production, replace the _fetch_* helpers with real HTTP calls to
OpenWeatherMap, WeatherAPI, etc. using httpx.AsyncClient.
"""

from datetime import datetime, timedelta
import random
import math
from typing import Optional

from app.models import (
    WeatherData,
    WeatherCondition,
    TemperatureUnit,
    AggregationType,
    ForecastDay,
)


# ── Simulated internal data ───────────────────────────────────────────────

_CITY_PRESETS: dict[str, dict] = {
    "london":   {"country": "GB", "base_temp": 12, "humidity": 72, "condition": WeatherCondition.CLOUDY},
    "paris":    {"country": "FR", "base_temp": 15, "humidity": 65, "condition": WeatherCondition.CLEAR},
    "tokyo":    {"country": "JP", "base_temp": 20, "humidity": 60, "condition": WeatherCondition.CLEAR},
    "new york": {"country": "US", "base_temp": 18, "humidity": 58, "condition": WeatherCondition.CLEAR},
    "sydney":   {"country": "AU", "base_temp": 22, "humidity": 55, "condition": WeatherCondition.CLEAR},
    "moscow":   {"country": "RU", "base_temp": 5,  "humidity": 70, "condition": WeatherCondition.SNOW},
    "dubai":    {"country": "AE", "base_temp": 35, "humidity": 30, "condition": WeatherCondition.CLEAR},
    "mumbai":   {"country": "IN", "base_temp": 30, "humidity": 80, "condition": WeatherCondition.RAIN},
    "berlin":   {"country": "DE", "base_temp": 10, "humidity": 68, "condition": WeatherCondition.CLOUDY},
    "cairo":    {"country": "EG", "base_temp": 28, "humidity": 25, "condition": WeatherCondition.CLEAR},
    "beijing":  {"country": "CN", "base_temp": 16, "humidity": 50, "condition": WeatherCondition.FOG},
    "rio":      {"country": "BR", "base_temp": 27, "humidity": 75, "condition": WeatherCondition.CLEAR},
    "toronto":  {"country": "CA", "base_temp": 8,  "humidity": 62, "condition": WeatherCondition.CLOUDY},
    "rome":     {"country": "IT", "base_temp": 19, "humidity": 55, "condition": WeatherCondition.CLEAR},
    "seoul":    {"country": "KR", "base_temp": 14, "humidity": 58, "condition": WeatherCondition.WINDY},
}

_UNKNOWN_CITIES: set[str] set()  # tracks cities that weren't in presets


def _celsius_to_fahrenheit(c: float) -> float:
    return round(c * 9 / 5 + 32, 1)


def _convert_temp(celsius: float, unit: TemperatureUnit) -> float:
    return _celsius_to_fahrenheit(celsius) if unit == TemperatureUnit.FAHRENHEIT else round(celsius, 1)


# ── Simulated fetch from "Source A" ───────────────────────────────────────

def _fetch_source_a(city: str, unit: TemperatureUnit) -> Optional[WeatherData]:
    """Simulate fetching from an external weather API (e.g. OpenWeatherMap)."""
    key = city.strip().lower()
    preset = _CITY_PRESETS.get(key)

    if preset:
        base_temp = preset["base_temp"] + random.uniform(-3, 3)
        condition = preset["condition"]
    else:
        # Generate plausible random data for unknown cities
        base_temp = random.uniform(-5, 38)
        condition = random.choice(list(WeatherCondition))

    humidity = int(max(0, min(100, (preset["humidity"] if preset else 50) + random.randint(-10, 10))))
    temp_c = round(base_temp, 1)
    feels_c = round(temp_c + random.uniform(-2, 2), 1)

    return WeatherData(
        city=city.strip().title(),
        country=preset["country"] if preset else None,
        temperature=_convert_temp(temp_c, unit),
        feels_like=_convert_temp(feels_c, unit),
        humidity=humidity,
        pressure=random.randint(990, 1030),
        wind_speed=round(random.uniform(0, 40), 1),
        condition=condition,
        description=condition.value.capitalize(),
        visibility=round(random.uniform(2, 20), 1),
        uv_index=round(random.uniform(0, 11), 1) if condition in (WeatherCondition.CLEAR, WeatherCondition.CLOUDY) else None,
        timestamp=datetime.utcnow(),
    )


# ── Public service functions ───────────────────────────────────────────────

async def get_weather(city: str, unit: TemperatureUnit = TemperatureUnit.CELSIUS) -> WeatherData:
    """Fetch current weather for a single city."""
    data = _fetch_source_a(city, unit)
    if data is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Could not retrieve weather data for '{city}'")
    return data


async def get_aggregated_weather(
    cities: list[str],
    aggregation: AggregationType,
    unit: TemperatureUnit,
) -> dict:
    """Fetch weather for multiple cities and compute aggregated statistics."""
    results: list[WeatherData] = []
    errors: list[str] = []

    for city in cities:
        try:
            data = await get_weather(city, unit)
            results.append(data)
        except ValueError:
            errors.append(city)

    if not results:
        raise ValueError(f"Could not retrieve data for any of the cities: {errors}")

    temps = [d.temperature for d in results]
    humidities = [d.humidity for d in results]
    wind_speeds = [d.wind_speed for d in results]
    pressures = [d.pressure for d in results]

    def _agg(values: list[float]) -> float:
        if aggregation == AggregationType.AVERAGE:
            return round(sum(values) / len(values), 1)
        elif aggregation == AggregationType.MIN:
            return round(min(values), 1)
        else:
            return round(max(values), 1)

    aggregated = {
        "temperature": _agg(temps),
        "humidity": _agg(humidities),
        "wind_speed": _agg(wind_speeds),
        "pressure": _agg(pressures),
        "skipped_cities": errors if errors else None,
    }

    return aggregated, results, errors


async def get_forecast(city: str, days: int, unit: TemperatureUnit) -> list[ForecastDay]:
    """Generate a simulated multi-day forecast."""
    key = city.strip().lower()
    preset = _CITY_PRESETS.get(key)
    base_temp = preset["base_temp"] if preset else 15

    forecast: list[ForecastDay] = []
    for i in range(1, days + 1):
        day_offset = random.uniform(-5, 5)
        high_c = base_temp + day_offset + random.uniform(2, 6)
        low_c = base_temp + day_offset - random.uniform(2, 6)
        condition = random.choice(list(WeatherCondition))

        forecast.append(
            ForecastDay(
                date=(datetime.utcnow() + timedelta(days=i)).strftime("%Y-%m-%d"),
                temp_high=_convert_temp(high_c, unit),
                temp_low=_convert_temp(low_c, unit),
                condition=condition,
                description=condition.value.capitalize(),
                precipitation_chance=random.randint(0, 100),
            )
        )

    return forecast

{"content":""""Pydantic models for request/response schemas."""

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, field_validator
from typing import Optional
from datetime import datetime
from enum import Enum


# ── Enums ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

class WeatherCondition(str, Enum):
    CLEAR = "clear"
    CLOUDY = "cloudy"
    RAIN = "rain"
    SNOW = "snow"
    STORM = "storm"
    FOG = "fog"
    WINDY = "windy"


class TemperatureUnit(str, Enum):
    CELSIUS = "celsius"
    FAHRENHEIT = "fahrenheit"


class AggregationType(str, Enum):
    AVERAGE = "average"
    MIN = "min"
    MAX = "max"


# ── Request Models ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

class WeatherRequest(BaseModel):
    """Request model for querying weather data by city."""
    city: str = Field(..., min_length=1, max_length=100, description="City name")
    country_code: Optional[str] = Field(
        None, min_length=2, max_length=2, description="ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code"
    )
    unit: TemperatureUnit = Field(TemperatureUnit.CELSIUS, description="Temperature unit")


class AggregationRequest(BaseModel):
    """Request model for aggregating weather across multiple cities."""
    cities: list[str] = Field(..., min_length=1, max_length=20, description="List of city names")
    aggregation: AggregationType = Field(
        AggregationType.AVERAGE, description="Aggregation method"
    )
    unit: TemperatureUnit = Field(TemperatureUnit.CELSIUS, description="Temperature unit")

    @field_validator("cities")
    @classmethod
    def cities_must_not_be_empty(cls, v: list[str]) -> list[str]:
        stripped = [c.strip() for c in v if c.strip()]
        if not stripped:
            raise ValueError("At least one non-empty city name is required")
        return stripped


# ── Response Models ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

class WeatherData(BaseModel):
    """Core weather data for a single location."""
    city: str
    country: Optional[str] = None
    temperature: float = Field(..., description="Temperature in requested unit")
    feels_like: float = Field(..., description="Feels-like temperature")
    humidity: int = Field(..., ge=0, le=100, description="Humidity percentage")
    pressure: int = Field(..., description="Atmospheric pressure in hPa")
    wind_speed: float = Field(..., ge=0, description="Wind speed in km/h")
    condition: WeatherCondition
    description: str
    visibility: Optional[float] = Field(None, ge=0, description="Visibility in km")
    uv_index: Optional[float] = Field(None, ge=0, description="UV index")
    timestamp: datetime


class WeatherResponse(BaseModel):
    """Single-city weather response."""
    success: bool = True
    data: WeatherData
    unit: TemperatureUnit
    source: str = Field(..., description="Data source identifier")


class AggregationResponse(BaseModel):
    """Multi-city aggregated weather response."""
    success: bool = True
    aggregation: AggregationType
    unit: TemperatureUnit
    aggregated: dict
    city_count: int
    cities: list[str]
    details: list[WeatherData]
    timestamp: datetime


class ForecastDay(BaseModel):
    """Single day forecast."""
    date: str
    temp_high: float
    temp_low: float
    condition: WeatherCondition
    description: str
    precipitation_chance: int = Field(..., ge=0, le=100)


class ForecastResponse(BaseModel):
    """Multi-day forecast response."""
    success: bool = True
    city: str
    unit: TemperatureUnit
    forecast: list[ForecastDay]


class ErrorResponse(BaseModel):
    """Standard error response."""
    success: bool = False
    error: str
    detail: Optional[str] = None
    status_code: int

from datetime import datetime, timedelta
import random
import math
from typing import Optional

from app.models import (
    WeatherData,
    WeatherCondition,
    TemperatureUnit,
    AggregationType,
    ForecastDay,
)


# ── Simulated internal data ───────────────────────────────────────────────

_CITY_PRESETS: dict[str, dict] = {
    "london":   {"country": "GB", "base_temp": 12, "humidity": 72, "condition": WeatherCondition.CLOUDY},
    "paris":    {"country": "FR", "base_temp": 15, "humidity": 65, "condition": WeatherCondition.CLEAR},
    "tokyo":    {"country": "JP", "base_temp": 20, "humidity": 60, "condition": WeatherCondition.CLEAR},
    "new york": {"country": "US", "base_temp": 18, "humidity": 58, "condition": WeatherCondition.CLEAR},
    "sydney":   {"country": "AU", "base_temp": 22, "humidity": 55, "condition": WeatherCondition.CLEAR},
    "moscow":   {"country": "RU", "base_temp": 5,  "humidity": 70, "condition": WeatherCondition.SNOW},
    "dubai":    {"country": "AE", "base_temp": 35, "humidity": 30, "condition": WeatherCondition.CLEAR},
    "mumbai":   {"country": "IN", "base_temp": 30, "humidity": 80, "condition": WeatherCondition.RAIN},
    "berlin":   {"country": "DE", "base_temp": 10, "humidity": 68, "condition": WeatherCondition.CLOUDY},
    "cairo":    {"country": "EG", "base_temp": 28, "humidity": 25, "condition": WeatherCondition.CLEAR},
    "beijing":  {"country": "CN", "base_temp": 16, "humidity": 50, "condition": WeatherCondition.FOG},
    "rio":      {"country": "BR", "base_temp": 27, "humidity": 75, "condition": WeatherCondition.CLEAR},
    "toronto":  {"country": "CA", "base_temp": 8,  "humidity": 62, "condition": WeatherCondition.CLOUDY},
    "rome":     {"country": "IT", "base_temp": 19, "humidity": 55, "condition": WeatherCondition.CLEAR},
    "seoul":    {"country": "KR", "base_temp": 14, "humidity": 58, "condition": WeatherCondition.WINDY},
}

_UNKNOWN_CITIES: set[str] set()  # tracks cities that weren't in presets


def _celsius_to_fahrenheit(c: float) -> float:
    return round(c * 9 / 5 + 32, 1)


def _convert_temp(celsius: float, unit: TemperatureUnit) -> float:
    return _celsius_to_fahrenheit(celsius) if unit == TemperatureUnit.FAHRENHEIT else round(celsius, 1)


# ── Simulated fetch from "Source A" ───────────────────────────────────────

def _fetch_source_a(city: str, unit: TemperatureUnit) -> Optional[WeatherData]:
    """Simulate fetching from an external weather API (e.g. OpenWeatherMap)."""
    key = city.strip().lower()
    preset = _CITY_PRESETS.get(key)

    if preset:
        base_temp = preset["base_temp"] + random.uniform(-3, 3)
        condition = preset["condition"]
    else:
        # Generate plausible random data for unknown cities
        base_temp = random.uniform(-5, 38)
        condition = random.choice(list(WeatherCondition))

    humidity = int(max(0, min(100, (preset["humidity"] if preset else 50) + random.randint(-10, 10))))
    temp_c = round(base_temp, 1)
    feels_c = round(temp_c + random.uniform(-2, 2), 1)

    return WeatherData(
        city=city.strip().title(),
        country=preset["country"] if preset else None,
        temperature=_convert_temp(temp_c, unit),
        feels_like=_convert_temp(feels_c, unit),
        humidity=humidity,
        pressure=random.randint(990, 1030),
        wind_speed=round(random.uniform(0, 40), 1),
        condition=condition,
        description=condition.value.capitalize(),
        visibility=round(random.uniform(2, 20), 1),
        uv_index=round(random.uniform(0, 11), 1) if condition in (WeatherCondition.CLEAR, WeatherCondition.CLOUDY) else None,
        timestamp=datetime.utcnow(),
    )


# ── Public service functions ───────────────────────────────────────────────

async def get_weather(city: str, unit: TemperatureUnit = TemperatureUnit.CELSIUS) -> WeatherData:
    """Fetch current weather for a single city."""
    data = _fetch_source_a(city, unit)
    if data is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Could not retrieve weather data for '{city}'")
    return data


async def get_aggregated_weather(
    cities: list[str],
    aggregation: AggregationType,
    unit: TemperatureUnit,
) -> dict:
    """Fetch weather for multiple cities and compute aggregated statistics."""
    results: list[WeatherData] = []
    errors: list[str] = []

    for city in cities:
        try:
            data = await get_weather(city, unit)
            results.append(data)
        except ValueError:
            errors.append(city)

    if not results:
        raise ValueError(f"Could not retrieve data for any of the cities: {errors}")

    temps = [d.temperature for d in results]
    humidities = [d.humidity for d in results]
    wind_speeds = [d.wind_speed for d in results]
    pressures = [d.pressure for d in results]

    def _agg(values: list[float]) -> float:
        if aggregation == AggregationType.AVERAGE:
            return round(sum(values) / len(values), 1)
        elif aggregation == AggregationType.MIN:
            return round(min(values), 1)
        else:
            return round(max(values), 1)

    aggregated = {
        "temperature": _agg(temps),
        "humidity": _agg(humidities),
        "wind_speed": _agg(wind_speeds),
        "pressure": _agg(pressures),
        "skipped_cities": errors if errors else None,
    }

    return aggregated, results, errors


async def get_forecast(city: str, days: int, unit: TemperatureUnit) -> list[ForecastDay]:
    """Generate a simulated multi-day forecast."""
    key = city.strip().lower()
    preset = _CITY_PRESETS.get(key)
    base_temp = preset["base_temp"] if preset else 15

    forecast: list[ForecastDay] = []
    for i in range(1, days + 1):
        day_offset = random.uniform(-5, 5)
        high_c = base_temp + day_offset + random.uniform(2, 6)
        low_c = base_temp + day_offset - random.uniform(2, 6)
        condition = random.choice(list(WeatherCondition))

        forecast.append(
            ForecastDay(
                date=(datetime.utcnow() + timedelta(days=i)).strftime("%Y-%m-%d"),
                temp_high=_convert_temp(high_c, unit),
                temp_low=_convert_temp(low_c, unit),
                condition=condition,
                description=condition.value.capitalize(),
                precipitation_chance=random.randint(0, 100),
            )
        )

    return forecast

- `AgentSessionServer`

The public runtime abstraction should be split into three layers.

### `AgentSessionServer`

Owns:

- create, load, join, leave, close, delete, and list sessions

- global server events
- session snapshots and deltas
- extension `broadcast()` state

- transport listeners that accept client connections and yield bidirectional channels

### `AgentSessionClient`

Owns:

- connecting to a running server through a transport
- listing, creating, joining, leaving, and deleting sessions
- subscribing to global server events
- subscribing to session-specific snapshots and deltas
- keeping synchronized session state caches for one or more sessions
- exposing a stable event API to interactive mode or web mode

### transport abstraction

Server side:

- listens for incoming client connections
- each accepted connection yields a bidirectional channel

Client side:

- connects to a server through a transport-specific address if needed
- yields the same kind of bidirectional channel

This should support:

- in-process
- stdio
- websocket
- any future transport that can provide the same channel semantics

The important point is that transport is not the architecture. It is just how server and client get a channel.

## Event scopes

The server has two conceptual event scopes with each client.

### Global server event scope

These are not tied to one joined session.

Examples:

- server connected
- server shutting down
- session created
- session deleted
- session archived or closed
- session list metadata changed
- session status changed, for example busy or idle
- global resource or provider changes, if exposed globally

These events let a client render things like:

- session picker
- recent sessions list
- status badges for sessions
- connection status

### Session-specific event scope

These are tied to one session.

Examples:

- initial session snapshot
- message start, update, end
- tool execution start, update, end
- queue updates
- compaction start, end
- retry start, end
- model changes
- thinking changes
- active tool changes
- tree navigation
- labels
- extension `broadcast()` updates
- extension `open()` handle traffic

A client may subscribe to one or more sessions. The renderer may only show one active session at a time, but the client design should allow keeping synchronized state for multiple sessions if needed later.

## Mutation flow

Clients must never mutate synchronized session state directly.

The flow is:

1. client subscribes to global events and joins or watches a session
2. server sends an initial snapshot for that session
3. client sends commands or intents to the server
4. server validates and applies authoritative mutations
5. server emits canonical deltas to subscribed clients, including the initiating client
6. clients update their synchronized caches from deltas only

The rule is:

- commands go up
- state deltas come down

This must work the same in local and remote mode.

- `resume_session`
- `fork_session`
- `import_session`

- `join_session`
- `leave_session`

Instead of replacing a local runtime host implicitly:

1. client sends a fork command against its active session, for example with an `entryId`
2. server forks that session and creates a new session id
3. server returns either:

4. client chooses to join that new session

A single client instance should be able to maintain:

- one global server state cache
- a map of synchronized session caches by session id

- session lists from global state
- keeping synchronized state for several sessions
- future tabbed or split views without redesigning the sync layer

## Implementation phases

## Phase 1. Centralize sync-visible state changes in `AgentSession`

Do first:

- move `user_bash` handling into `AgentSession`
- add missing session sync events
- make `AgentSession` emit all session-visible mutations

Do not start by changing transport.

## Phase 2. Build `AgentSessionServer` next to the existing runtime host

Build a new server abstraction next to the current local-only runtime and host code.

Responsibilities:

- maintain multiple sessions and runtimes
- expose global and session-scoped sync
- produce snapshots and deltas
- provide transport-agnostic channel handling

The current `AgentSessionRuntimeHost` can remain in place temporarily for existing local interactive mode while the new server is implemented and compared against it.

## Phase 3. Build `AgentSessionClient`

Build a new client abstraction next to the current direct interactive-mode integration.

Responsibilities:

- connect through a pluggable transport
- subscribe to global server events
- subscribe to session snapshots and deltas
- send session lifecycle and mutation commands
- keep synchronized state caches

## Phase 4. Make a new interactive mode consume the client

Refactor by adding a new interactive mode path that:

- talks only to `AgentSessionClient`
- issues commands to the server
- rerenders from synchronized state
- stops directly driving session-visible refresh logic

The old interactive mode can remain temporarily as a reference during migration.

{"path":"plans/pi-session-sync-unification.md","edits":[{"oldText":"## Mutation flow

Clients must never mutate synchronized session state directly.
","newText":"## Connection model

The server should expose two conceptual communication scopes to each client:

- global server scope
- session-specific scope

These do not need two physical sockets or two different transports. One underlying connection can carry both, as long as every message is clearly scoped.

For example, one transport channel can carry:

- global events and global commands
- session snapshot and session deltas for one or more session ids
- session commands addressed to a specific session id

This keeps transport simple while preserving a clean architectural split.

## Command scopes

Commands should also be split by scope.

### Global commands

Examples:

- list sessions
- create session
- delete session
- join session
- leave session
- watch session
- unwatch session
- reload global resources, if exposed globally

### Session commands

Examples:

- prompt
- abort
- set model
- set thinking level
- set active tools
- navigate tree
- compact
- run bash
- extension UI event
- extension UI close

A client may keep one active session for the renderer, but commands should still be explicit about which session they target. That keeps the protocol correct when a client watches multiple sessions at once.

## Mutation flow

Clients must never mutate synchronized session state directly.
"}]}

The server should expose two conceptual communication scopes to each client:

- global server scope
- session-specific scope

These do not need two physical sockets or two different transports. One underlying connection can carry both, as long as every message is clearly scoped.

For example, one transport channel can carry:

- global events and global commands
- session snapshot and session deltas for one or more session ids
- session commands addressed to a specific session id

This keeps transport simple while preserving a clean architectural split.

## Command scopes

Commands should also be split by scope.

### Global commands

Examples:

- list sessions
- create session
- delete session
- join session
- leave session
- watch session
- unwatch session
- reload global resources, if exposed globally

### Session commands

Examples:

- prompt
- abort
- set model
- set thinking level
- set active tools
- navigate tree
- compact
- run bash
- extension UI event
- extension UI close

A client may keep one active session for the renderer, but commands should still be explicit about which session they target. That keeps the protocol correct when a client watches multiple sessions at once.

## Mutation flow

Clients must never mutate synchronized session state directly.
"}]}

function.description: Manage background processes started with terminal(background=true). Actions: 'list' (show all), 'poll' (check status + new output), 'log' (full output with pagination), 'wait' (block until done or timeout), 'kill' (terminate), 'write' (send raw stdin data without newline), 'submit' (send data + Enter, for answering prompts).

context.description: Number of context lines before and after each match (grep mode only)

function.name: terminal
function.description:
Execute shell commands on a Linux environment. Filesystem usually persists between calls.

Do NOT use cat/head/tail to read files — use read_file instead.
Do NOT use grep/rg/find to search — use search_files instead.
Do NOT use ls to list directories — use search_files(target='files') instead.

Background: ONLY for long-running servers, watchers, or processes that never exit. Do NOT use vim/nano/interactive tools without pty=true — they hang without a pseudo-terminal. Pipe git output to cat if it might page.

{"path":"json_config_parser.py","content":"#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
JSON API Configuration Parser

Parses JSON API responses and extracts configuration values with support for:
  - Dot-notation key paths (e.g. "database.host")
  - Default values for missing keys
  - Type validation and coercion
  - Nested / flattened extraction
  - Environment variable overrides
  - Multiple API sources (URLs or local files)
"""

import json
import os
import sys
import logging
import argparse
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Optional, Union
from urllib.request import urlopen, Request
from urllib.error import URLError, HTTPError

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Logging
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
logging.basicConfig(
    level=logging.INFO,
    format="%(asctime)s [%(levelname)s] %(message)s",
)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Core: resolve a dot-notation path inside a nested dict
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def resolve_path(data: dict, path: str, default: Any = None) -> Any:
    """
    Walk *data* along a dot-separated *path* and return the value.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> resolve_path({"a": {"b": 1}}, "a.b")
    1
    >>> resolve_path({"a": {"b": 1}}, "a.c", default="missing")
    'missing'
    """
    keys = path.split(".")
    current = data
    for key in keys:
        if isinstance(current, dict) and key in current:
            current = current[key]
        else:
            return default
    return current


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Type validators / coercers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

VALIDATORS = {
    "str":   (str,  lambda v: str(v)),
    "int":   (int,  lambda v: int(v)),
    "float": (float, lambda v: float(v)),
    "bool":  (bool, lambda v: v if isinstance(v, bool) else str(v).lower() in ("true", "1", "yes")),
    "list":  (list, lambda v: v if isinstance(v, list) else json.loads(v)),
}


def validate_type(value: Any, expected_type: str) -> Any:
    """
    Validate / coerce *value* to *expected_type*.

    Raises ``ValueError`` when coercion fails.
    """
    if expected_type not in VALIDATORS:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown type '{expected_type}'. Choose from: {list(VALIDATORS)}")

    py_type, coercer = VALIDATORS[expected_type]

    if isinstance(value, py_type):
        return value

    try:
        return coercer(value)
    except Exception as exc:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Cannot coerce {value!r} to {expected_type}: {exc}"
        ) from exc


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# JSON loading helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def load_json_from_file(filepath: str) -> dict:
    """Read and parse a JSON file from the local filesystem."""
    path = Path(filepath)
    if not path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config file not found: {filepath}")
    with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        return json.load(fh)


def load_json_from_url(url: str, headers: Optional[dict] = None, timeout: int = 10) -> dict:
    """Fetch and parse a JSON response from an HTTP(S) endpoint."""
    req = Request(url, headers=headers or {})
    try:
        with urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as resp:
            return json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))
    except HTTPError as exc:
        raise RuntimeError(f"HTTP {exc.code} fetching {url}") from exc
    except URLError as exc:
        raise RuntimeError(f"URL error fetching {url}: {exc.reason}") from exc


def load_json(source: str, headers: Optional[dict] = None, timeout: int = 10) -> dict:
    """
    Load JSON from *source* which may be:
      - a file path  (exists on disk)
      - an HTTP(S) URL
      - '-' for stdin
    """
    if source == "-":
        return json.load(sys.stdin)

    if Path(source).exists():
        return load_json_from_file(source)

    if source.startswith(("http://", "https://")):
        return load_json_from_url(source, headers=headers, timeout=timeout)

    # Last resort: try to parse the string itself as JSON
    try:
        return json.loads(source)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Source '{source}' is neither a file, URL, nor valid JSON string"
        )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Configuration extractor
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class ConfigExtractor:
    """
    High-level helper that loads one or more JSON sources and extracts
    configuration values according to a spec.

    Parameters
    ----------
    sources : list[str]
        File paths, URLs, or raw JSON strings (loaded in order; later
        sources override earlier ones).
    env_override : bool
        If ``True``, environment variables matching the uppercased key path
        (with dots replaced by underscores) take precedence over JSON values.
        E.g. key ``database.host`` → env var ``DATABASE_HOST``.
    headers : dict | None
        Optional HTTP headers when fetching from URLs.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        sources: list[str],
        env_override: bool = False,
        headers: Optional[dict] = None,
    ):
        self.env_override = env_override
        self.headers = headers
        self.merged: dict = {}
        for src in sources:
            data = load_json(src, headers=self.headers)
            self.merged = self._deep_merge(self.merged, data)

    # ---- internal helpers ------------------------------------------------

    @staticmethod
    def _deep_merge(base: dict, override: dict) -> dict:
        """Recursively merge *override* into *base*."""
        result = base.copy()
        for key, value in override.items():
            if key in result and isinstance(result[key], dict) and isinstance(value, dict):
                result[key] = ConfigExtractor._deep_merge(result[key], value)
            else:
                result[key] = value
        return result

    def _env_key(self, path: str) -> str:
        return path.upper().replace(".", "_")

    # ---- public API ------------------------------------------------------

    def get(self, path: str, default: Any = None, expected_type: Optional[str] = None) -> Any:
        """
        Extract the value at *path* (dot-notation).

        If *env_override* is enabled the corresponding env-var wins.
        If *expected_type* is given the value is validated / coerced.
        """
        value = resolve_path(self.merged, path, default=default)

        if self.env_override:
            env_val = os.environ.get(self._env_key(path))
            if env_val is not None:
                value = env_val

        if expected_type is not None and value is not None:
            value = validate_type(value, expected_type)

        return value

    def get_many(self, specs: list[dict]) -> dict:
        """
        Extract multiple values at once.

        Each spec dict supports the keys:
          - key   (str)           : dot-notation path  (required)
          - default (any)         : fallback value      (optional)
          - type  (str)           : expected type name   (optional)
          - alias (str)           : rename the output key (optional)

        Returns a flat dict of {alias_or_key: value}.
        """
        result: dict = {}
        for spec in specs:
            key = spec["key"]
            alias = spec.get("alias", key)
            default = spec.get("default")
            expected_type = spec.get("type")
            result[alias] = self.get(key, default=default, expected_type=expected_type)
        return result

    def flatten(self, prefix: str = "", sep: str = ".") -> dict:
        """Return a fully flattened dict with dot-notation keys."""
        out: dict = {}

        def _walk(obj: Any, path: str) -> None:
            if isinstance(obj, dict):
                for k, v in obj.items():
                    _walk(v, f"{path}{sep}{k}" if path else k)
            else:
                out[path] = obj

        _walk(self.merged, prefix)
        return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CLI
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Parse JSON API responses and extract configuration values.",
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
        epilog="""\
examples:
  # Extract a single value from a local file
  python json_config_parser.py config.json -k database.host

  # Extract from a remote API with an auth header
  python json_config_parser.py https://api.example.com/config \
      --header "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN" -k app.port --type int

  # Merge two sources, extract multiple keys
  python json_config_parser.py defaults.json overrides.json \
      -k database.host -k database.port --type int

  # Allow environment variable overrides
  python json_config_parser.py config.json -k debug --type bool --env-override

  # Flatten all keys
  python json_config_parser.py config.json --flatten
""",
    )

    p.add_argument(
        "sources",
        nargs="+",
        help="One or more JSON sources: file paths, HTTP(S) URLs, or '-' for stdin.",
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "-k", "--key",
        action="append",
        default=[],
        dest="keys",
        help="Dot-notation key path to extract (repeatable).",
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "--default",
        action="append",
        default=[],
        dest="defaults",
        help="Default value for the corresponding --key (positional match).",
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "--type",
        action="append",
        default=[],
        dest="types",
        choices=list(VALIDATORS),
        help="Enforce type for the corresponding --key (positional match).",
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "--header",
        action="append",
        default=[],
        dest="headers",
        help='HTTP header in "Name: Value" form (repeatable).',
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "--env-override",
        action="store_true",
        default=False,
        help="Allow env vars (e.g. DATABASE_HOST) to override JSON values.",
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "--flatten",
        action="store_true",
        default=False,
        help="Print all config values as a flattened key=value list.",
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "--output-json",
        action="store_true",
        default=False,
        help="Output results as a JSON object instead of key=value lines.",
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "-v", "--verbose",
        action="store_true",
        default=False,
        help="Enable debug logging.",
    )
    return p


def main(argv: Optional[list[str]] = None) -> None:
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)

    if args.verbose:
        logging.getLogger().setLevel(logging.DEBUG)

    # Parse HTTP headers
    headers: dict = {}
    for hdr in args.headers:
        if ":" not in hdr:
            logger.error("Invalid header format (expected 'Name: Value'): %s", hdr)
            sys.exit(1)
        name, _, value = hdr.partition(":")
        headers[name.strip()] = value.strip()

    # Build extractor
    extractor = ConfigExtractor(
        sources=args.sources,
        env_override=args.env_override,
        headers=headers or None,
    )

    # --flatten mode
    if args.flatten:
        flat = extractor.flatten()
        if args.output_json:
            print(json.dumps(flat, indent=2))
        else:
            for k, v in sorted(flat.items()):
                print(f"{k}={v!r}")
        return

    # No keys → dump the whole merged object
    if not args.keys:
        if args.output_json:
            print(json.dumps(extractor.merged, indent=2))
        else:
            print(json.dumps(extractor.merged, indent=2))
        return

    # Extract requested keys
    results: dict = {}
    for idx, key in enumerate(args.keys):
        default = args.defaults[idx] if idx < len(args.defaults) else None
        expected_type = args.types[idx] if idx < len(args.types) else None

        try:
            value = extractor.get(key, default=default, expected_type=expected_type)
        except ValueError as exc:
            logger.error("Type error for key '%s': %s", key, exc)
            sys.exit(1)

        results[key] = value

    if args.output_json:
        print(json.dumps(results, indent=2))
    else:
        for key, value in results.items():
            print(f"{key}={value!r}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
"}

{"path":"json_config_parser.py","content":"#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
JSON API Configuration Parser

Parses JSON API responses and extracts configuration values with support for:
  - Dot-notation key paths (e.g. "database.host")
  - Default values for missing keys
  - Type validation and coercion
  - Nested / flattened extraction
  - Environment variable overrides
  - Multiple API sources (URLs or local files)
"""

import json
import os
import sys
import logging
import argparse
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Optional, Union
from urllib.request import urlopen, Request
from urllib.error import URLError, HTTPError

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Logging
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
logging.basicConfig(
    level=logging.INFO,
    format="%(asctime)s [%(levelname)s] %(message)s",
)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Core: resolve a dot-notation path inside a nested dict
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def resolve_path(data: dict, path: str, default: Any = None) -> Any:
    """
    Walk *data* along a dot-separated *path* and return the value.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> resolve_path({"a": {"b": 1}}, "a.b")
    1
    >>> resolve_path({"a": {"b": 1}}, "a.c", default="missing")
    'missing'
    """
    keys = path.split(".")
    current = data
    for key in keys:
        if isinstance(current, dict) and key in current:
            current = current[key]
        else:
            return default
    return current


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Type validators / coercers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

VALIDATORS = {
    "str":   (str,  lambda v: str(v)),
    "int":   (int,  lambda v: int(v)),
    "float": (float, lambda v: float(v)),
    "bool":  (bool, lambda v: v if isinstance(v, bool) else str(v).lower() in ("true", "1", "yes")),
    "list":  (list, lambda v: v if isinstance(v, list) else json.loads(v)),
}


def validate_type(value: Any, expected_type: str) -> Any:
    """
    Validate / coerce *value* to *expected_type*.

    Raises ``ValueError`` when coercion fails.
    """
    if expected_type not in VALIDATORS:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown type '{expected_type}'. Choose from: {list(VALIDATORS)}")

    py_type, coercer = VALIDATORS[expected_type]

    if isinstance(value, py_type):
        return value

    try:
        return coercer(value)
    except Exception as exc:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Cannot coerce {value!r} to {expected_type}: {exc}"
        ) from exc


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# JSON loading helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def load_json_from_file(filepath: str) -> dict:
    """Read and parse a JSON file from the local filesystem."""
    path = Path(filepath)
    if not path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config file not found: {filepath}")
    with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        return json.load(fh)


def load_json_from_url(url: str, headers: Optional[dict] = None, timeout: int = 10) -> dict:
    """Fetch and parse a JSON response from an HTTP(S) endpoint."""
    req = Request(url, headers=headers or {})
    try:
        with urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as resp:
            return json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))
    except HTTPError as exc:
        raise RuntimeError(f"HTTP {exc.code} fetching {url}") from exc
    except URLError as exc:
        raise RuntimeError(f"URL error fetching {url}: {exc.reason}") from exc


def load_json(source: str, headers: Optional[dict] = None, timeout: int = 10) -> dict:
    """
    Load JSON from *source* which may be:
      - a file path  (exists on disk)
      - an HTTP(S) URL
      - '-' for stdin
    """
    if source == "-":
        return json.load(sys.stdin)

    if Path(source).exists():
        return load_json_from_file(source)

    if source.startswith(("http://", "https://")):
        return load_json_from_url(source, headers=headers, timeout=timeout)

    # Last resort: try to parse the string itself as JSON
    try:
        return json.loads(source)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Source '{source}' is neither a file, URL, nor valid JSON string"
        )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Configuration extractor
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class ConfigExtractor:
    """
    High-level helper that loads one or more JSON sources and extracts
    configuration values according to a spec.

    Parameters
    ----------
    sources : list[str]
        File paths, URLs, or raw JSON strings (loaded in order; later
        sources override earlier ones).
    env_override : bool
        If ``True``, environment variables matching the uppercased key path
        (with dots replaced by underscores) take precedence over JSON values.
        E.g. key ``database.host`` → env var ``DATABASE_HOST``.
    headers : dict | None
        Optional HTTP headers when fetching from URLs.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        sources: list[str],
        env_override: bool = False,
        headers: Optional[dict] = None,
    ):
        self.env_override = env_override
        self.headers = headers
        self.merged: dict = {}
        for src in sources:
            data = load_json(src, headers=self.headers)
            self.merged = self._deep_merge(self.merged, data)

    # ---- internal helpers ------------------------------------------------

    @staticmethod
    def _deep_merge(base: dict, override: dict) -> dict:
        """Recursively merge *override* into *base*."""
        result = base.copy()
        for key, value in override.items():
            if key in result and isinstance(result[key], dict) and isinstance(value, dict):
                result[key] = ConfigExtractor._deep_merge(result[key], value)
            else:
                result[key] = value
        return result

    def _env_key(self, path: str) -> str:
        return path.upper().replace(".", "_")

    # ---- public API ------------------------------------------------------

    def get(self, path: str, default: Any = None, expected_type: Optional[str] = None) -> Any:
        """
        Extract the value at *path* (dot-notation).

        If *env_override* is enabled the corresponding env-var wins.
        If *expected_type* is given the value is validated / coerced.
        """
        value = resolve_path(self.merged, path, default=default)

        if self.env_override:
            env_val = os.environ.get(self._env_key(path))
            if env_val is not None:
                value = env_val

        if expected_type is not None and value is not None:
            value = validate_type(value, expected_type)

        return value

    def get_many(self, specs: list[dict]) -> dict:
        """
        Extract multiple values at once.

        Each spec dict supports the keys:
          - key   (str)           : dot-notation path  (required)
          - default (any)         : fallback value      (optional)
          - type  (str)           : expected type name   (optional)
          - alias (str)           : rename the output key (optional)

        Returns a flat dict of {alias_or_key: value}.
        """
        result: dict = {}
        for spec in specs:
            key = spec["key"]
            alias = spec.get("alias", key)
            default = spec.get("default")
            expected_type = spec.get("type")
            result[alias] = self.get(key, default=default, expected_type=expected_type)
        return result

    def flatten(self, prefix: str = "", sep: str = ".") -> dict:
        """Return a fully flattened dict with dot-notation keys."""
        out: dict = {}

        def _walk(obj: Any, path: str) -> None:
            if isinstance(obj, dict):
                for k, v in obj.items():
                    _walk(v, f"{path}{sep}{k}" if path else k)
            else:
                out[path] = obj

        _walk(self.merged, prefix)
        return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CLI
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Parse JSON API responses and extract configuration values.",
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
        epilog="""\
examples:
  # Extract a single value from a local file
  python json_config_parser.py config.json -k database.host

  # Extract from a remote API with an auth header
  python json_config_parser.py https://api.example.com/config \
      --header "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN" -k app.port --type int

  # Merge two sources, extract multiple keys
  python json_config_parser.py defaults.json overrides.json \
      -k database.host -k database.port --type int

  # Allow environment variable overrides
  python json_config_parser.py config.json -k debug --type bool --env-override

  # Flatten all keys
  python json_config_parser.py config.json --flatten
""",
    )

    p.add_argument(
        "sources",
        nargs="+",
        help="One or more JSON sources: file paths, HTTP(S) URLs, or '-' for stdin.",
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "-k", "--key",
        action="append",
        default=[],
        dest="keys",
        help="Dot-notation key path to extract (repeatable).",
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "--default",
        action="append",
        default=[],
        dest="defaults",
        help="Default value for the corresponding --key (positional match).",
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "--type",
        action="append",
        default=[],
        dest="types",
        choices=list(VALIDATORS),
        help="Enforce type for the corresponding --key (positional match).",
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "--header",
        action="append",
        default=[],
        dest="headers",
        help='HTTP header in "Name: Value" form (repeatable).',
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "--env-override",
        action="store_true",
        default=False,
        help="Allow env vars (e.g. DATABASE_HOST) to override JSON values.",
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "--flatten",
        action="store_true",
        default=False,
        help="Print all config values as a flattened key=value list.",
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "--output-json",
        action="store_true",
        default=False,
        help="Output results as a JSON object instead of key=value lines.",
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "-v", "--verbose",
        action="store_true",
        default=False,
        help="Enable debug logging.",
    )
    return p


def main(argv: Optional[list[str]] = None) -> None:
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)

    if args.verbose:
        logging.getLogger().setLevel(logging.DEBUG)

    # Parse HTTP headers
    headers: dict = {}
    for hdr in args.headers:
        if ":" not in hdr:
            logger.error("Invalid header format (expected 'Name: Value'): %s", hdr)
            sys.exit(1)
        name, _, value = hdr.partition(":")
        headers[name.strip()] = value.strip()

    # Build extractor
    extractor = ConfigExtractor(
        sources=args.sources,
        env_override=args.env_override,
        headers=headers or None,
    )

    # --flatten mode
    if args.flatten:
        flat = extractor.flatten()
        if args.output_json:
            print(json.dumps(flat, indent=2))
        else:
            for k, v in sorted(flat.items()):
                print(f"{k}={v!r}")
        return

    # No keys → dump the whole merged object
    if not args.keys:
        if args.output_json:
            print(json.dumps(extractor.merged, indent=2))
        else:
            print(json.dumps(extractor.merged, indent=2))
        return

    # Extract requested keys
    results: dict = {}
    for idx, key in enumerate(args.keys):
        default = args.defaults[idx] if idx < len(args.defaults) else None
        expected_type = args.types[idx] if idx < len(args.types) else None

        try:
            value = extractor.get(key, default=default, expected_type=expected_type)
        except ValueError as exc:
            logger.error("Type error for key '%s': %s", key, exc)
            sys.exit(1)

        results[key] = value

    if args.output_json:
        print(json.dumps(results, indent=2))
    else:
        for key, value in results.items():
            print(f"{key}={value!r}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
"}

Actions: 'list' (show all), 'poll' (check status + new output), 'log' (full output with pagination), 'wait' (block until done or timeout), 'kill' (terminate), 'write' (send raw stdin data without newline), 'submit' (send data + Enter, for answering prompts).

action.description: Action to perform on background processes

session_id.description: Process session ID (from terminal background output). Required for all actions except 'list'.

data.description: Text to send to process stdin (for 'write' and 'submit' actions)

timeout.description: Max seconds to block for 'wait' action. Returns partial output on timeout.

offset.description: Line offset for 'log' action (default: last 200 lines)

limit.description: Max lines to return for 'log' action

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with line numbers and pagination. Use this instead of cat/head/tail in terminal. Output format: 'LINE_NUM|CONTENT'. Suggests similar filenames if not found. Use offset and limit for large files. Reads exceeding ~100K characters are rejected; use offset and limit to read specific sections of large files. NOTE: Cannot read images or binary files — use vision_analyze for images.

path.description: Path to the file to read (absolute, relative, or ~/path)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed, default: 1)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read (default: 500, max: 2000)

function.name: search_files
function.description:
Search file contents or find files by name. Use this instead of grep/rg/find/ls in terminal. Ripgrep-backed, faster than shell equivalents.

Content search (target='content'): Regex search inside files. Output modes: full matches with line numbers, file paths only, or match counts.

File search (target='files'): Find files by glob pattern (e.g., '*.py', '*config*'). Also use this instead of ls — results sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: Regex pattern for content search, or glob pattern (e.g., '*.py') for file search

target.description: 'content' searches inside file contents, 'files' searches for files by name

path.description: Directory or file to search in (default: current working directory)

file_glob.description: Filter files by pattern in grep mode (e.g., '*.py' to only search Python files)

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 50)

offset.description: Skip first N results for pagination (default: 0)

output_mode.description: Output format for grep mode: 'content' shows matching lines with line numbers, 'files_only' lists file paths, 'count' shows match counts per file

context.description: Number of context lines before and after each match (grep mode only)

function.name: terminal
function.description:
Execute shell commands on a Linux environment. Filesystem usually persists between calls.

Do NOT use cat/head/tail to read files — use read_file instead.
Do NOT use grep/rg/find to search — use search_files instead.
Do NOT use ls to list directories — use search_files(target='files') instead.
Do NOT use sed/awk to edit files — use patch instead.
Do NOT use echo/cat heredoc to create files — use write_file instead.
Reserve terminal for: builds, installs, git, processes, scripts, network, package managers, and anything that needs a shell.

Foreground (default): Commands return INSTANTLY when done, even if the timeout is high. Set timeout=300 for long builds/scripts — you'll still get the result in seconds if it's fast. Prefer foreground for everything that finishes.
Background: ONLY for long-running servers, watchers, or processes that never exit. Set background=true to get a session_id, then use process(action="wait") to block until done — it returns instantly on completion, same as foreground. Use process(action="poll") only when you need a progress check without blocking.
Do NOT use background for scripts, builds, or installs — foreground with a generous timeout is always better (fewer tool calls, instant results).
Working directory: Use 'workdir' for per-command cwd.
PTY mode: Set pty=true for interactive CLI tools (Codex, Claude Code, Python REPL).

Do NOT use vim/nano/interactive tools without pty=true — they hang without a pseudo-terminal. Pipe git output to cat if it might page.
Important: cloud sandboxes may be cleaned up, idled out, or recreated between turns. Persistent filesystem means files can resume later; it does NOT guarantee a continuously running machine or surviving background processes. Use terminal sandboxes for task work, not durable hosting.

command.description: The command to execute on the VM

background.description: ONLY for servers/watchers that never exit. For scripts, builds, installs — use foreground with timeout instead (it returns instantly when done).

timeout.description: Max seconds to wait (default: 180). Returns INSTANTLY when command finishes — set high for long tasks, you won't wait unnecessarily.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command (absolute path). Defaults to the session working directory.

check_interval.description: Seconds between automatic status checks for background processes (gateway/messaging only, minimum 30). When set, I'll proactively report progress.

pty.description: Run in pseudo-terminal (PTY) mode for interactive CLI tools like Codex, Claude Code, or Python REPL. Only works with local and SSH backends. Default: false.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Write content to a file, completely replacing existing content. Use this instead of echo/cat heredoc in terminal. Creates parent directories automatically. OVERWRITES the entire file — use 'patch' for targeted edits.

path.description: Path to the file to write (will be created if it doesn't exist, overwritten if it does)

content.description: Complete content to write to the file

function.name: clarify

- You want to offer to save a skill or update memory

function.name: delegate_task
function.description:
Spawn one or more subagents to work on tasks in isolated contexts. Each subagent gets its own conversation, terminal session, and toolset. Only the final summary is returned -- intermediate tool results never enter your context window.

TWO MODES (one of 'goal' or 'tasks' is required):
1. Single task: provide 'goal' (+ optional context, toolsets)
2. Batch (parallel): provide 'tasks' array with up to 3 items. All run concurrently and results are returned together.

WHEN TO USE delegate_task:
- Reasoning-heavy subtasks (debugging, code review, research synthesis)
- Tasks that would flood your context with intermediate data
- Parallel independent workstreams (research A and B simultaneously)

WHEN NOT TO USE (use these instead):
- Mechanical multi-step work with no reasoning needed -> use execute_code
- Single tool call -> just call the tool directly
- Tasks needing user interaction -> subagents cannot use clarify

IMPORTANT:
- Subagents have NO memory of your conversation. Pass all relevant info (file paths, error messages, constraints) via the 'context' field.
- Subagents CANNOT call: delegate_task, clarify, memory, send_message, execute_code.
- Each subagent gets its own terminal session (separate working directory and state).
- Results are always returned as an array, one entry per task.

goal.description: What the subagent should accomplish. Be specific and self-contained -- the subagent knows nothing about your conversation history.

context.description: Background information the subagent needs: file paths, error messages, project structure, constraints. The more specific you are, the better the subagent performs.

toolsets.description: Toolsets to enable for this subagent. Default: inherits your enabled toolsets. Common patterns: ['terminal', 'file'] for code work, ['web'] for research, ['terminal', 'file', 'web'] for full-stack tasks.

goal.description: Task goal

context.description: Task-specific context

toolsets.description: Toolsets for this specific task

tasks.description: Batch mode: up to 3 tasks to run in parallel. Each gets its own subagent with isolated context and terminal session. When provided, top-level goal/context/toolsets are ignored.
